name: Presence
description: The exit half of the animation story: it keeps rendering its child with `present: false` until the child's own CSS says its transition is over, and only then lets React remove it. `startingStyle` is the entrance and needs no JavaScript at all — this is the ~1 KB the other direction costs, because React unmounts synchronously and there is nothing left to transition.

props.name: present
props.description: Whether the child should be there. The exit starts the moment this goes false.

props.name: children
props.description: The subtree, told which way it is going.

a11y: The exit is measured from the element's own `transition-duration`/`animation-duration`, so `prefers-reduced-motion` — which zeroes `--transitionTime` — removes the node in the same commit with no opt-in.
`data-state` is `'open'` or `'closed'` on the child, which is what a CSS exit selects on. A node on its way out is still in the accessibility tree, so anything hiding it has to say so itself.
